primaryFacts.claim: Mass fraction is constituent mass divided by the sum of the masses of all constituents, including the named constituent.
primaryFacts.supportType: defining table formula and SI unit; all constituents confirmed by NIST mass-of-mixture definition in section 8.6.10

primaryFacts.claim: Volume fraction uses constituent volumes prior to mixing, divided by their sum.

primaryFacts.claim: Using a measured final mixture volume as the denominator changes the reference quantity; no additivity assumption is required by the IUPAC volume-fraction definition.
primaryFacts.supportType: explicit derivation from prior-to-mixing definition and separate mixture-volume V in concentration rows; no numerical contraction claim checked

primaryFacts.claim: Both fractions have dimension one. Percent has value 10^-2, so a fraction f is written numerically as 100*f followed by percent.
primaryFacts.supportType: dimensionless-quantity discussion, fractions named, percent table value

primaryFacts.claim: The pure-substance molar volumes used for volume fraction refer to the same temperature and pressure; summation includes all substances.
primaryFacts.shortExactExcerpt: at the same temperature and pressure
primaryFacts.supportType: explicit official NIST definition; equivalence to V_i/sum_j V_j follows with V_i=n_i*V_m,i and x_i=n_i/sum_j n_j
